title: Outlook for Mac: Purview DLP wait-on-send support
summary: Hold: the DLP rule command is still missing parts of Microsoft's documented warn-dialog example, including the user-notification action. The roadmap facts and the distinction between documented Windows controls and unconfirmed Mac settings are supported.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Learn does not yet document the Mac wait-on-send feature or its enabling and timeout settings.
claims.quote: Searched: "Outlook for Mac" "wait-on-send"; DLPWaitOnSendEnabled admin center UI Outlook Mac registry dlpwaitonsendtimeout. Read mobile/macOS policy-tip reference, classic and new Windows references, and Set-OrganizationConfig; no Mac wait-on-send configuration found.

claims.claim: Set-OrganizationConfig -DLPWaitOnSendEnabled $true -DLPWaitOnSendTimeout <seconds> configures the documented Exchange Online organisation control.
claims.quote: $true: Mail sent from Outlook for Windows to Exchange is evaluated by DLP. To set the timeout value, use the DLPWaitOnSendTimeout parameter.

claims.claim: No admin-centre path is documented for the Exchange wait-on-send parameters.
claims.quote: Searched: "DLPWaitOnSendEnabled" "admin center"; DLPWaitOnSendEnabled admin center UI Outlook Mac registry dlpwaitonsendtimeout. Read Set-OrganizationConfig and dlp-policy-reference-new-outlook; the latter says the experience is controlled solely through the Exchange parameters.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Exchange parameters are documented for new Outlook for Windows, but their application to Mac is unconfirmed.
claims.quote: Searched: "Outlook for Mac" "wait-on-send"; DLPWaitOnSendEnabled admin center UI Outlook Mac registry dlpwaitonsendtimeout. Read dlp-policy-reference-new-outlook and Set-OrganizationConfig: Windows support stated; neither states Mac applicability.

claims.where: controls[1].note and scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The policy-tips policy can target individual users or groups.
claims.quote: You can target policies to individuals or groups, so you can test and deploy policy tip UI as needed through your organization.

claims.claim: Policy-tip UI is off by default for Android, iOS and macOS until its admin policy is enabled.
claims.quote: Policy Tip UI is turned off by default in Outlook for Android, iOS, and macOS to allow for administrators to test and perform user training prior to deployment.

claims.claim: The documented policy-tips switch is a policy-tip UI control, not a documented wait-on-send switch.
claims.quote: To enable Policy Tip UI to appear in Outlook for Android, iOS, and macOS, you must enable the policy listed in the following section in the Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center.

claims.claim: The documented entry point for configuring the DLP policy is Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls: DLP rule API cell
claims.claim: The printed New-DlpComplianceRule call is a complete documented call for creating the pre-send dialog rule.
claims.quote: Set the User notifications toggle to On. New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <DLP Rule Name> -Policy <DLP Policy Name> -NotifyUser Owner -NotifyPolicyTipDisplayOption "Dialog"
claims.fix: Replace the call in both front matter and the rendered table with the full documented warn-rule example: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <name> -Policy <policy> -NotifyUser Owner -NotifyPolicyTipDisplayOption "Dialog" -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @(@{operator="And";groups=@(@{operator="Or";name="Default";labels=@(@{name=<GUID>;type="Sensitivity"})})}) -ExceptIfRecipientDomainIs @("contoso.com","microsoft.com"). The current call omits the notification action and the example's trusted-domain exception; mentioning -NotifyUser Owner in a note does not put it in the runnable call. Keep the existing caveat that Mac dialog support is unconfirmed. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-osp-get-started.

claims.claim: Microsoft's warn-rule example sets -NotifyUser Owner.
claims.quote: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <DLP Rule Name> -Policy <DLP Policy Name> -NotifyUser Owner -NotifyPolicyTipDisplayOption "Dialog"

claims.claim: The cited Outlook for Microsoft 365 dialog procedure does not confirm Mac pre-send dialog support.
claims.quote: Searched: "Outlook for Mac" "wait" "DLP" default timeout roles; Microsoft Purview data loss prevention licensing Outlook Mac wait on send oversharing service description. Read dlp-osp-get-started and mobile/macOS reference; oversharing sections name Microsoft 365 or Android/iOS, not Mac.

claims.claim: Outlook for Microsoft 365 wait on send is configured with the dlpwaitonsendtimeout registry key.
claims.quote: After you've configured the Oversharing dialog, you can optionally enable the Wait on send dialog feature using the dlpwaitonsendtimeout Registry key (DWORD value).

claims.claim: The corresponding Group Policy setting is named Specify wait time to evaluate sensitive content.
claims.quote: You can set this RegKey via group policy, Specify wait time to evaluate sensitive content, script, or other mechanism for configuring registry keys.

claims.claim: The mobile/macOS reference's wait-on-send section says Android and iOS do not yet support it, without naming macOS in that statement.
claims.quote: Outlook for Android and iOS doesn't yet support DLP Wait-to-Send

claims.claim: For Outlook for Microsoft 365 without wait on send configured, the message sends immediately and DLP subsequently evaluates and applies policy actions.
claims.quote: The email message is sent immediately once Send is clicked. The DLP data classification service evaluates the message and apply the actions defined in the DLP policy.

claims.claim: For Outlook for Microsoft 365, a configured wait from 0 to 9999 seconds offers Send anyway if evaluation has not completed in that time.
claims.quote: If the policy evaluation doesn't complete in the specified time a Send anyway button appears allowing the user to bypass the presend check. The T value range is 0 to 9999 seconds.

claims.claim: For Outlook for Microsoft 365, a configured value greater than 9999 is replaced with 10000.
claims.quote: If the T value is greater than 9999, it's replaced with 10000

claims.claim: That greater-than-9999 configuration holds the message until evaluation finishes without a Send Anyway override.
claims.quote: the Send Anyway button doesn't appear. This holds the message until the policy evaluation completes and doesn't provide the user with an override option.

claims.claim: In new Outlook for Windows, a zero timeout immediately shows Send Anyway.
claims.quote: When DLPWaitOnSendTimeout = 0, user will immediately see "Send Anyway" in the infobar of mail.

claims.claim: Learn says matched block rules block the message regardless of how Policy tips is configured.
claims.quote: If the block rules defined in the DLP policy are met, the message will be blocked regardless of how Policy tips is configured.

claims.claim: The planned change adds evaluation to the user's email-sending workflow rather than initiating messages autonomously.
claims.quote: Organizations can require a DLP evaluation before an email is sent and configure how long users must wait for policy evaluation to complete.

claims.claim: For Outlook for Microsoft 365, evaluation duration can vary with internet speed, content length and policy count.
claims.quote: The duration for completing the evaluation can vary depending on factors such as internet speed, content length, and the number of policies defined.
